mainTopic: עירוב תחומין for שבת next to יום טוב: one קדושה or two, רב's ruling, and רבה's rule of הכנה tested by אביי
overview: This amud deals with עירוב תחומין when שבת and יום טוב (or two days of יום טוב) fall back to back, and asks whether they are one קדושה or two. A ברייתא ends with a doubtful view in which the person is 'a donkey driver and a camel driver' and must be strict both ways. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל then say one עירוב covers both days. רב rules like 'four זקנים' and like רבי אליעזר that the days are שתי קדושות, and the גמרא defends his list: it reverses the names in the ברייתא, reads them as agreeing with רבי, and says רב had a direct tradition. רב חסדא then points out that רב also forbade an egg laid on one day on the other, which sounds like one קדושה. רבה answers that the egg is forbidden because of הכנה, since one holy day may not prepare for another, and a ברייתא backs this rule. אביי tests the rule of הכנה several times, and רבה answers each challenge: the עירוב takes effect at the start of שבת, the food must be fit while it is still day, the two עירובין sit 1,000 אמות out, and an עירוב made with one's feet needs only silent sitting, which works even according to the רבנן. The amud ends as רבה בר רב חנין begins quoting a ברייתא against רבה, and that quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Stuck between two directions
steps.stepSummary: The end of an opinion in the ברייתא: because we are unsure whether the two days are one קדושה or two, the person must be strict both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: This person is like a donkey driver and a camel driver at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle. This line ends the previous opinion, which says the person is caught between two possibilities and must follow the stricter side of each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey driver walks behind his animal, and a camel driver walks in front, so someone doing both is pulled in opposite directions. Since we do not know if the first day's עירוב still works on the second day, he may only walk where he would be allowed under both possibilities.

keyTerms.meaning: Donkey driver, who walks behind the animal
Camel driver, who walks in front of the animal
Setting up a Shabbat 'home base' somewhere else, so you can walk 2000 אמות from that spot

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'חמר גמל' as a ruling about animals. It is an image for being stuck between two opposite directions, meaning he must keep both sets of limits.

phrases.english: This one is a donkey driver and a camel driver.
phrases.notes: He is pulled two ways, so he is strict on both sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends an opinion in the ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is unclear whether the two days are one קדושה or two, the person must be strict according to both possibilities.

steps.title: Two sages: one עירוב covers both days
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל say the first day's עירוב carries over to the second day, as written in this version of the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, say: if he made an עירוב with his feet for the first day, he does not need to make one with his feet for the second day. If his עירוב food was eaten on the first day, he may still rely on it on the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion in the ברייתא. These two sages treat the two days as one unit, so one עירוב works for both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to make an עירוב: standing at the spot in person ('with his feet'), or placing food there. In both cases, this opinion says what was set up for day one still counts on day two, even if the food is already gone. That only makes sense if the two days are one קדושה.

keyTerms.meaning: Made an עירוב 'with his feet': went to the spot in person and declared it his Shabbat base
His עירוב food was eaten
He may go out (walk) based on it

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is the source of the contradiction the גמרא raises in step 6.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, say:
If he made an eiruv with his feet for the first day,
he does not make an eiruv with his feet for the second day;
phrases.notes: The first one still works.

phrases.english: if his eiruv was eaten on the first day,
he goes out based on it on the second day.
phrases.notes: The עירוב already took effect for both days.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further opinion in the same ברייתא, taking the 'one קדושה' side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two days are one קדושה, so the first day's עירוב works for the second day too.

steps.title: רב rules: two separate קדושות
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like the four זקנים and like רבי אליעזר, who holds the two days are שתי קדושות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the הלכה follows these four Elders, and follows רבי אליעזר, who said they are two separate holinesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the practical ruling: the two days are separate, as רבי אליעזר holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Two קדושות' means each day stands alone. So a person may even make a different עירוב for each day, and one day's עירוב does not automatically cover the other. רב says four זקנים agree with this view.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows
Elders, senior sages
According to the view of
Two separate holinesses, so each day stands on its own

steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling: the הלכה is שתי קדושות, like רבי אליעזר and the four זקנים.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The halakha is like these four Elders,
and in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer,
who said they are two holinesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הֲלָכָה כְּאַרְבָּעָה זְקֵנִים הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from quoting the ברייתא to a practical ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is that the two days are שתי קדושות.

steps.title: Who are the four זקנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא names the four זקנים whom רב follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the four Elders: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, רבי אליעזר son of רבי שמעון, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה, the 'unnamed one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly whom רב meant by 'these four זקנים.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice that the first two names are the same sages from step 2. This list is what sets up the problem in step 6. רבי יוסי בר יהודה is called סתימתאה because many of his teachings were recorded without his name.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The unnamed one': a sage whose views were often recorded anonymously
Son of רבי

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר בן רבי שמעון in this list is a different person from רבי אליעזר in step 3, whose view רב follows.

phrases.english: And these are the four Elders:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka
and Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Shimon
and Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda, the 'unnamed one.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the 'four זקנים' mentioned in רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four זקנים are רשב"ג, רבי ישמעאל בן רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, רבי אליעזר בן רבי שמעון, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה.

steps.title: Another version of the list
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבי אלעזר is one of the four in place of רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: one of them is רבי אלעזר, and they take out רבי יוסי בר יהודה, the 'unnamed one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of who the four זקנים are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one name changes: רבי אלעזר replaces רבי יוסי בר יהודה. The first two names, which matter for the next question, stay the same in both versions.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say (another version)
One of them
Removes, takes out

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
one of them is Rabbi Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַפֵּיק רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה סְתִימְתָּאָה.
phrases.english: and they remove Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda, the 'unnamed one.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of the list in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the alternate version, רבי אלעזר replaces רבי יוסי בר יהודה among the four.

steps.title: But these two sages said the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: רשב"ג and רבי ישמעאל said in the ברייתא that the two days are one קדושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we heard that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה hold the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between רב's list and the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says these sages hold שתי קדושות. Yet in step 2 they said the first day's עירוב covers the second day, which is the 'one קדושה' view. Both cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
The opposite
We have heard them say

phrases.english: But Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
we heard them say the opposite!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בַּר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אִיפְּכָא שָׁמְעִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the list of four זקנים with the ברייתא quoted earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that רשב"ג and רבי ישמעאל hold שתי קדושות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא they let the first day's עירוב work for the second day, which only fits the 'one קדושה' view.

steps.title: Reverse the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by switching the names in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying the ברייתא's names must be switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the names are reversed, רשב"ג and רבי ישמעאל hold the stricter view: a new עירוב is needed for the second day, and an eaten עירוב does not help. That is the שתי קדושות view, so רב's list and the ברייתא now agree.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it, switch the attributions

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא is read with the names switched, so רשב"ג and רבי ישמעאל hold שתי קדושות, matching רב's ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: 'איפוך' does not cancel the ruling. It only changes which sage said which opinion in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Reverse it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: switching the attributions in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא as quoted has רשב"ג and רבי ישמעאל holding one קדושה.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the names reversed, they hold שתי קדושות, matching רב's four זקנים.

steps.title: After the switch, they seem to agree with רבי
steps.stepSummary: If we switch the names, רשב"ג and רבי ישמעאל now say exactly what רבי said, so what is the argument?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, isn't this the same as רבי's view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the name-switch from Step 7. Once we switch the names, the 'other side' of the ברייתא says the same thing as רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא normally presents two sides arguing. After the switch, רשב"ג and רבי ישמעאל hold שתי קדושות, which is רבי's own view. So the switch seems to erase the argument the ברייתא was built to show.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your answer is true)
That is the same as
רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: If so,
this is the same as Rabbi!
phrases.notes: After the switch, the opinions are identical.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 7 (switching the names).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Switching the names leaves no disagreement, but the ברייתא is written as an argument.

steps.title: Read it as 'and so too said רבן שמעון בן גמליאל'
steps.stepSummary: Reread the ברייתא so that רשב"ג is agreeing with רבי, not arguing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: 'And so too said רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how we read the ברייתא. רשב"ג is now presented as agreeing with רבי, not disagreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the ברייתא must be an argument. The answer drops that assumption: the line is a statement of agreement ('וכן אמר'). This makes the switch from Step 7 fit smoothly.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way)
And so too said (wording that shows agreement)
Etc., and so on

phrases.english: Say:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And so too said Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, etc.
phrases.notes: Agreement, not dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text (from dispute to agreement)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא presents two opposing sides, so the switch makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא lists רשב"ג as agreeing with רבי.

steps.title: Why not count רבי among the elders?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי also holds שתי קדושות, why didn't רב list him with the four זקנים?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let רב also count רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב's list of four זקנים leaves out רבי, since רבי says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 listed exactly four זקנים. If רבי clearly holds this view in the ברייתא, he should be a fifth. Leaving him out suggests something is off.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him count
Also

phrases.english: Then let him also count Rabbi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 9: if רבי holds this view, he belongs on the list.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's list of exactly four זקנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי holds the same view, so he should be counted too.

steps.title: רבי taught it but did not hold it
steps.stepSummary: רבי passed this view on from his teachers, but it was not his own opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי taught it, but did not hold it himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי was only passing on what he learned. It was not his personal view, so he is not counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between teaching a view and holding it. רבי recorded his teachers' position, but he personally disagreed. So רב's list includes only people who actually held the view.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught it (passed it on)
But he did not hold it (it was not his opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that whoever says a teaching in a ברייתא holds it himself. Sometimes a תנא only passes on what he received.

phrases.english: Rabbi taught it
but did not hold it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי תָּנֵי לַהּ וְלָא סָבַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between teaching a view and holding it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's statement in the ברייתא shows his own opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי only passed on his teachers' view, so he is not on רב's list.

steps.title: Maybe the other רבנן also only taught it
steps.stepSummary: If רבי only taught the view, maybe the other זקנים also only taught it without holding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the רבנן also taught it and did not hold it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last answer around. If teaching does not prove holding, how do we know any of the four זקנים held this view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 11 creates a new problem. If a statement can be 'just teaching,' then the sources for רב's four זקנים might also be only teaching. So רב's whole list would be in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis (here, the other זקנים such as רשב"ג and רבי ישמעאל)
They hold it

phrases.english: The Rabbis also taught it
and did not hold it?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן נָמֵי תָּנוּ לַהּ וְלָא סָבְרִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of Step 11 against רב's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: How רב knows the four זקנים actually held the view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If teaching does not prove holding for רבי, it does not prove it for the others either.

steps.title: רב had a direct tradition
steps.stepSummary: רב did not learn this from the wording of the sources. He had a received tradition about what the four זקנים held.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב learned it as a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב knew the four זקנים' view from a tradition passed down to him, not from reading the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question attacked the sources, saying the wording proves nothing. The answer says רב did not depend on the wording at all. He had a clear tradition that these four held שתי קדושות.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned it as a received tradition

steps.whatToRemember: רב's list of four זקנים stands: רבי only passed the view on, while רב knew from a direct tradition that the four זקנים truly held שתי קדושות.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'גמרא' does not mean the תלמוד. It means a tradition received from one's teachers.

phrases.english: Rav learned it as a received tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12 and closes the defense of רב's list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's list depends on the wording of ברייתות, which could be 'teaching only.'
steps.terutzMaskana: רב knew the four זקנים' view from a direct tradition.

steps.title: רב חסדא begins to contradict רב's rulings
steps.stepSummary: After רב הונא died, רב חסדא came to point out a contradiction between two statements of רב. He starts by quoting רב's ruling about the four זקנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא passed away, רב חסדא came in to raise a contradiction from רב against רב: Did רב really say the הלכה follows the four זקנים and רבי אליעזר, who says they are שתי קדושות?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא is setting up a contradiction, and this line gives only its first side: רב's ruling that the two days are שתי קדושות. The second side comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא defended רב's ruling. Now רב חסדא will show that רב said something else that seems to clash with it. This line only states the first ruling, framed as a question ('Did רב really say...?').

keyTerms.meaning: When he passed away (literally, when his soul rested)
רב's leading student
An אמורא, student of רב
To raise a contradiction between one statement of רב and another
Two separate holinesses (שבת and יום טוב count as separate)

steps.whyThisMatters: It opens a new challenge to רב's ruling from a different angle: not the sources, but רב's own consistency.

phrases.english: When Rav Huna passed away,
Rav Chisda entered
to raise a contradiction between Rav and Rav.
Did Rav say:
The halacha follows the four Elders,
and in line with Rabbi Eliezer,
who said they are two sanctities?
phrases.notes: First side of the contradiction. The second side follows next.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָיֵיל רַב חִסְדָּא לְמִירְמָא דְּרַב אַדְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge after the defense of רב's list ended in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the halacha follows the four זקנים (שתי קדושות)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This sets up a clash with another statement of רב, which will be quoted next.

steps.title: רב's ruling on the egg seems to treat the two days as one
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא completes his contradiction. רב said an egg laid on שבת or יום טוב is forbidden on the next day. That suggests one sanctity, which clashes with רב's ruling that they are שתי קדושות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it stated: when שבת and יום טוב come one after the other, רב said that an egg laid on one day is forbidden on the other day!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings the second statement of רב, which seems to contradict the ruling quoted in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An egg laid on יום טוב is forbidden on that same day. If it stays forbidden on the next day too, it sounds as if both days count as one long holy day (קדושה אחת). But רב already ruled like the four זקנים that they are שתי קדושות, so his two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it stated? This opens a contradiction from another teaching.
It was born, meaning the egg was laid.
On this one, on that one. It refers to the two holy days.
שבת and יום טוב falling on back-to-back days.

steps.confusionAlert: Everyone agrees that an egg laid on יום טוב is forbidden on that same day. The question here is only why it stays forbidden on the next day. That detail is what makes it sound like one sanctity.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated:
Shabbat and Yom Tov (on consecutive days),
phrases.notes: Either order: יום טוב then שבת, or שבת then יום טוב.

phrases.english: Rav said:
[an egg] laid on this one is forbidden on that one!
phrases.notes: This implies one sanctity, which contradicts רב's ruling of שתי קדושות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction that רב חסדא began setting up in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the הלכה follows the four זקנים, who hold שתי קדושות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidding the egg on the second day seems to assume one sanctity, which contradicts שתי קדושות.

steps.title: The egg is forbidden because of preparation, not one sanctity
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the egg is forbidden on the second day because of the rule of הכנה. You may not prepare on one holy day for another. The two days can still be שתי קדושות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: there, the egg is forbidden because of preparation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה resolves the contradiction by giving a different reason for the egg ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The egg ruling does not prove that the days are one sanctity. The egg is forbidden because the first holy day would be 'preparing' it for the second holy day, and that is not allowed. So רב can hold שתי קדושות and still forbid the egg.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in the case of the egg.
Preparation. One day getting something ready for another day.
The אמורא who gives the answer.

steps.whyThisMatters: The reason behind a law matters. Two rulings that look contradictory can rest on different reasons.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
There, [it is forbidden] because of preparation.
phrases.notes: The egg is forbidden because of הכנה, not because the days are one sanctity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason. The ruling rests on a separate law, so it does not contradict.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The egg ruling shows that רב treats the two days as one sanctity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The egg is forbidden because of הכנה, and the days remain שתי קדושות.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that one holy day may not prepare for another
steps.stepSummary: רבה's idea is backed by a ברייתא. It learns from the verse 'on the sixth day they shall prepare' that only a weekday may prepare for שבת or יום טוב. יום טוב may not prepare for שבת, and שבת may not prepare for יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'And it shall be on the sixth day that they shall prepare.' A weekday prepares for שבת, and a weekday prepares for יום טוב. But יום טוב does not prepare for שבת, and שבת does not prepare for יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that the rule of הכנה really exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the מן says the preparing for שבת happens on the sixth day, a regular weekday. From this the ברייתא learns that only a weekday may prepare. So an egg laid on one holy day cannot be used on the next one.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא.
And they shall prepare. This is the word in the verse.
A regular weekday.
Prepares.

steps.whatToRemember: A weekday may prepare for a holy day, but one holy day may not prepare for another. That is why the egg is forbidden on the second day.

phrases.english: As it was taught [in a ברייתא]:
"And it shall be on the sixth day, that they shall prepare"
phrases.notes: שמות ט״ז:ה׳, about the מן.

phrases.english: a weekday prepares for Shabbat
and a weekday prepares for Yom Tov,
but Yom Tov does not prepare for Shabbat
and Shabbat does not prepare for Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's answer in step 16 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a rule against הכנה from one holy day to another.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא expounding the verse in שמות ט״ז:ה׳.

steps.title: The עירוב in our משנה seems to be preparing from יום טוב for שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with our משנה. When יום טוב falls on Friday, a person sets up his עירוב on יום טוב so that it works for שבת. That looks like preparing on יום טוב for שבת, which רבה says is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But what about what we learned in the משנה? How does he do it? He brings the עירוב there on the first day, waits with it until dark, then takes it and goes. On the second day he waits with it until dark, then may eat it and go. Here he is preparing from יום טוב for שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's idea of הכנה from a case in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes יום טוב on Friday. On Friday afternoon, which is יום טוב, the person brings the עירוב back so it will take effect for שבת. If יום טוב may not prepare for שבת, how is that allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: That we learned in a משנה.
How does he do it?
He brings it, meaning the eruv.
He stays with it until nightfall.
The אמורא who challenges רבה.

steps.confusionAlert: 'The first' and 'the second' mean the eve of each day. On the second time, Friday afternoon, it is already יום טוב. That is exactly why אביי says יום טוב is preparing for שבת.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
But what about that which we learned [in the משנה]:
How does he do it?
He brings it [on the eve of] the first day,
and stays with it until nightfall,
and takes it and goes on his way.
On the second [day's eve] he stays with it until nightfall,
phrases.notes: This is Friday afternoon, which is already יום טוב.

phrases.english: and he may eat it and go on his way.

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא מֵכִין מִיּוֹם טוֹב לְשַׁבָּת!
phrases.english: Here he is preparing from Yom Tov for Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, אֶלָּא הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer of הכנה from steps 16 and 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that Yom Tov may not prepare for Shabbat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows setting up the eruv on Yom Tov for Shabbat, and that is a form of הכנה.

steps.title: The עירוב takes effect at the start of שבת, so שבת prepares for itself
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי: the עירוב acquires at the beginning of שבת, not at the end of יום טוב. So no preparation is done on יום טוב for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: Do you think the עירוב takes effect at the end of the day (on יום טוב)? The עירוב takes effect at the beginning of the day (the first moment of שבת), and שבת is allowed to prepare for itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his rule of הכנה against אביי's question about making an עירוב on יום טוב for שבת. He explains that the עירוב does not actually 'work' on יום טוב at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed that the עירוב sets up the new 'home base' at the last moment of יום טוב, which would be יום טוב preparing for שבת. רבה says the עירוב only takes hold at the first moment of שבת. Preparing on שבת for שבת itself is no problem, so the rule of הכנה is not broken.

keyTerms.meaning: The end of the day: the last moment before the holy day begins
The beginning of the day: the first moment of the holy day
The עירוב 'acquires', meaning it sets up the person's legal resting place
Prepares for itself: שבת's own preparation for שבת, which is allowed

steps.confusionAlert: Placing the food happens on יום טוב, but רבה says the legal effect happens on שבת. The physical act and the legal moment are not the same thing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the core assumption that the next two challenges will test: what exactly must be true at each moment for an עירוב to be valid.

phrases.english: Rabba said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מִי סָבְרַתְּ סוֹף הַיּוֹם קוֹנֶה עֵירוּב?
phrases.english: Do you think that the end of the day acquires the eruv?
phrases.notes: The end of the day here means the end of יום טוב.

phrases.english: The beginning of the day acquires the eruv,
phrases.notes: The beginning of the day here means the first moment of שבת.

phrases.english: and Shabbat prepares for itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the moment the עירוב takes legal effect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עירוב takes effect at the end of יום טוב, so it would count as יום טוב preparing for שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עירוב takes effect at the start of שבת, so שבת prepares for itself and there is no forbidden הכנה.

steps.title: If so, an עירוב should work with wine that only becomes permitted at night
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges: if the עירוב only needs to work at the start of the next day, then wine that becomes permitted at nightfall should be usable for an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: (אביי asked:) But if so, people should be able to make an עירוב with the flasks of wine. That wine only becomes permitted to drink once night falls.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's new idea by pointing to a known case where an עירוב is invalid. That case should be valid if רבה is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known case of a flask of wine that is still טבל, unfixed produce that may not be eaten. The flask only becomes permitted at nightfall through a תרומת מעשר set aside to take effect then. The הלכה is that this wine cannot serve as an עירוב. But if the עירוב only needs to work at the beginning of the new day, the wine is permitted by then, so why should it be invalid?

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: it introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
A flask or jug, here of wine
Produce from which the required gifts have not yet been taken, so it is forbidden to eat
The tithe-of-the-tithe given to a כהן, which must be removed before the produce is permitted

phrases.english: But if so, from now on
phrases.notes: אביי is the speaker, though he is not named.

phrases.english: let them make an eruv with the flasks?
phrases.notes: This refers to wine that becomes permitted only at nightfall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a problematic consequence from רבה's answer in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the עירוב takes effect at the beginning of the day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only the first moment of the new day matters, wine that is permitted by that moment should be valid. Yet it is known to be invalid.

steps.title: An עירוב needs food that is edible while it is still day
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the flask case fails for a different reason. The עירוב food must be fit to eat before the day ends, and this wine is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We require a meal that is fit to eat while it is still day, and here there is none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the flask case is invalid for a separate reason, not because of when the עירוב takes effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the עירוב 'acquires' at the start of the new day, there is a second requirement. The food must already be edible during the day before. The wine is still טבל until nightfall, so it fails that requirement. רבה's idea is untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal that is fit, meaning food that may legally be eaten
While it is still day, before the holy day begins
There is none: the requirement is missing

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate rules here. The moment of acquiring is the start of the new day. But the food must also be usable before that moment. Do not merge them.

phrases.english: We require a meal that is fit
while it is still day, and there is none.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעִינַן סְעוּדָה הָרְאוּיָה מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם, וְלֵיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's flask challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different reason explains the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The flask is invalid because the עירוב must work at the end of the day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The flask is invalid because the food must be edible while it is still day, a separate requirement.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's two עירובין seem to lack a meal usable while it is still day
steps.stepSummary: אביי uses the new rule against רבי אליעזר's משנה. A person may make two עירובין for יום טוב next to שבת, yet the second עירוב seems unusable during the first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what we learned in the משנה? רבי אליעזר says: when יום טוב is next to שבת, whether before it or after it, a person may make two עירובין. But we need a meal fit to eat while it is still day, and here there is none!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי first quotes רבי אליעזר's ruling, then turns the rule from step 21 against it. The answer to the flask case seems to create a new problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי אליעזר, a person can make one עירוב in one direction for the first day and another in the opposite direction for the second day. On the first day, he is limited to 2,000 אמות from his first עירוב, so he cannot reach the second one. The second עירוב is therefore not 'fit to eat while it is still day', so how can it be valid?

keyTerms.meaning: That we learned in a משנה
A יום טוב right next to שבת, before it or after it
Two עירובין, one for each day, possibly in different directions

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge tests whether 'fit while still day' means only legally permitted or also physically reachable.

phrases.english: But that which we learned:
phrases.notes: אביי is still the speaker.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
A Festival adjacent to Shabbat,
whether before it or after it,
a person may make two eruvin.
But don't we require a meal that is fit
while it is still day, and there is none!
phrases.notes: On the first day he cannot reach the second עירוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the requirement from step 21 against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement of סעודה הראויה מבעוד יום, as applied to רבי אליעזר's two עירובין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second עירוב cannot be reached during the first day, so it is not fit while it is still day. Yet רבי אליעזר validates it.

steps.title: The two עירובין are only a thousand אמות from town
steps.stepSummary: The answer to the challenge from רבי אליעזר's משנה: the two עירובין are placed 1,000 אמות from town in each direction, not 2,000. So the second עירוב is still within reach on the first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think he put one עירוב 2,000 אמות out on this side and the other 2,000 אמות out on that side? No. He put one 1,000 אמות out on this side and the other 1,000 אמות out on that side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge from step 22 by changing how we picture the case. The two עירובין are closer to town than אביי assumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed the two עירובין were 2,000 אמות out on opposite sides, so they would be 4,000 אמות apart. That would mean the second עירוב is out of reach on the first day. If each one is only 1,000 אמות out, they are 2,000 אמות apart. Then on the first day he can still reach the second עירוב, so it is usable before the day ends.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (a phrase that brings up a mistaken assumption in order to reject it)
2,000 אמות, the normal distance one may walk outside town on שבת or יום טוב
1,000 אמות
in this direction... in that direction

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the person gets to walk 4,000 אמות in one day. Each עירוב is only 1,000 אמות from town, so the two of them are exactly 2,000 אמות apart. From the first עירוב he can still reach the second one.

phrases.english: Do you think that he placed it
at the end of two thousand cubits in this direction,
and at the end of two thousand cubits in that direction?
No, it is that he placed it
at the end of one thousand cubits in this direction,
and at the end of one thousand cubits in that direction.
phrases.notes: The two עירובין are 2,000 אמות apart, so the second one is reachable on the first day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי סָבְרַתְּ דְּמַנַּח לֵיהּ בְּסוֹף אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכָאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by redefining where the עירובין were placed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing (אוקימתא): redefines the distances in the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each עירוב sits 2,000 אמות out on opposite sides, so the second is unreachable on day one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each עירוב sits 1,000 אמות out, so the second one is reachable and fit for use on day one.

steps.title: רב יהודה's ruling seems to require preparing on יום טוב for שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה from רב יהודה. He rules that whichever way a person made his עירוב on the first day, by walking or with bread, he makes it the same way for the second day. Setting it up for day two happens on day one, which looks like preparing on יום טוב for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רב יהודה said? If he made his עירוב with his feet on the first day, he makes it with his feet on the second day. If he made it with bread on the first day, he makes it with bread on the second day. Then he is preparing on יום טוב for שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new source, רב יהודה's ruling, to attack רבה's view that one may not prepare on יום טוב for שבת. To set up the second day's עירוב, the person must go out to the spot during the first day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב is next to שבת, each day can need its own עירוב. רב יהודה lets the person repeat the same method for the second day. But that means going out during the first day, which is יום טוב, to set up the עירוב for שבת. That is exactly the kind of preparation רבה forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: he made an עירוב with his feet: he walked to the spot himself and set his Shabbat residence there instead of placing food
he made an עירוב with bread: he placed food at the spot
first day / second day
preparing on יום טוב for שבת, which רבה holds is forbidden
But what about this...? (opens a challenge from another source)

phrases.english: But what about that which Rav Yehuda said:
If he made an eruv with his feet for the first day,
he makes an eruv with his feet for the second day;
if he made an eruv with bread on the first day,
he makes an eruv with bread on the second day.

phrases.aramaic: הָא קָא מֵכִין מִיּוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת!
phrases.english: But he is preparing from Yom Tov for Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 23 resolved the challenge from רבי אליעזר's משנה, אביי opens a new attack on the same principle using an אמורא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that one may not prepare on יום טוב for שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה lets a person set up the second day's עירוב in the same way as the first. That requires going out on day one (יום טוב) to set up for day two (שבת), which is forbidden preparation.

steps.title: He walks there silently and sits
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that making an עירוב with one's feet requires no words and no act. The person goes, stays quiet, and sits, so nothing counts as preparing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think he has to go and say something? He just goes, stays quiet, and sits there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's challenge from רב יהודה. Setting up an עירוב with one's feet involves no declaration or real action, so it is not preparation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed the person must actively set up his residence, for example by announcing "my residence is here." רבה says no declaration is needed. Simply being present at the spot is enough. Quietly going and sitting does not count as forbidden preparation on יום טוב for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: goes and says something, like a verbal declaration
stays silent
sits

phrases.english: He said to him:
Do you think that he goes and says something?
He goes, stays silent, and sits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the act: no declaration or action is involved, so it is not preparation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Making an עירוב by foot requires going and making a declaration, which counts as preparing.
steps.terutzMaskana: He goes silently and sits. Being present at the spot acquires the residence on its own, and that is not considered preparing.

steps.title: רבה's answer only fits רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whose view רבה's answer follows. He shows that it matches רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who holds that ownerless objects acquire a Shabbat residence. So רבה seems to depend on a disputed opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is like רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who said that ownerless objects acquire a שבת residence.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks which תנא holds that a person can acquire his Shabbat spot just by being there, without saying anything. He answers that it is רבי יוחנן בן נורי. This suggests רבה's answer rests on a debated view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If silent presence is enough, then residence is acquired automatically, without any intention or action. That is רבי יוחנן בן נורי's position: even ownerless objects, which no one sets up, acquire a שביתה. He also applies this to a person who is asleep. Other תנאים disagree, so רבה's answer now looks tied to only one side of a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom? (asks which authority a ruling follows)
a תנא who holds that Shabbat residence can be acquired automatically
ownerless objects
acquire a Shabbat residence, a fixed place from which their 2,000 אמות are measured

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the question of הכנה to the deeper question of how שביתה is acquired: automatically, or through a person's active intention.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri, who said:
Ownerless objects acquire a Shabbat residence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of רבה's answer in step 25 by tying it to a single, disputed תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's answer that silent presence is enough to acquire the residence
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Acquiring residence with no words or action only works if שביתה is acquired automatically. That is רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view, so רבה's answer seems limited to his opinion.

steps.title: רבה's view works even according to the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבה says his answer does not depend on רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The רבנן only disagree about a sleeping person, who cannot speak. An awake person could speak, so his silence counts as if he had spoken.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say my view follows the רבנן, they argue with רבי יוחנן בן נורי only about a sleeping person, who cannot say anything. But a person who is awake could speak if he wanted to. So even though he did not speak, he is treated like someone who did.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's question from Step 26. He shows that his view is not tied to רבי יוחנן בן נורי's disputed opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed that acquiring a שביתה without saying anything only works according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי. רבה narrows the argument. The רבנן disagree only when the person could not speak at all, like someone asleep. An awake person who stays quiet but could speak is treated as if he spoke, so all opinions agree with רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sleeping person, who cannot speak or form an intention
A person who is awake
He is able to say it
He is treated like someone who said it
They only disagree about this much (a phrase that limits how far an argument goes)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the awake person is acquiring his place by actually speaking. He says nothing at all. The point is only that he COULD speak, so the law treats his silence as if he had spoken.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רבה's answer from Step 25 alive. The person can still acquire his שביתה without speaking, so nothing counts as preparing on יום טוב for שבת.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows the Rabbis,
the Rabbis only disagree
phrases.notes: A limiting phrase: the argument goes only this far.

phrases.english: with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri
regarding a sleeping person, who cannot speak.
But regarding one who is awake,
since if he wanted to speak, he could speak
even though he did not speak,
he is considered like one who did speak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26's claim that רבה depends on the disputed view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the dispute: the רבנן disagree only about someone who cannot speak.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Acquiring a שביתה without words seemed to work only according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.terutzMaskana: An awake person who could speak counts as if he spoke, so everyone agrees with רבה.

steps.title: רבה בר רב חנין begins a challenge from a ברייתא about walking in one's field
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב חנין tells אביי that רבה would not have said this if he had known a certain ברייתא. The ברייתא forbids walking to the end of one's field on שבת to see what work it needs. The quote continues into the next passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב חנין said to אביי: If the Master had heard what was taught in a ברייתא, that a person may not walk to the end of his field to see what it needs, and similarly...
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up a new challenge. רבה בר רב חנין begins quoting a ברייתא to show that even walking without words can count as forbidden preparation. The quote and its point continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said that walking and sitting silently is not preparing. The ברייתא shows that walking alone can be forbidden when it serves a later purpose: here, checking a field for work to do after שבת. The words 'If the Master had heard' imply that רבה would have taken back his view had he known this source.

keyTerms.meaning: If the Master had heard (implying he would have changed his view)
That which was taught in a ברייתא
He may not walk
Similarly; in the same way

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is not finished here. Do not try to find the full challenge on this amud. The rest of the ברייתא comes in the next one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב חָנִין לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Chanin said to Abaye:
If the Master had heard
phrases.notes: "The Master" refers to רבה.

phrases.english: that which was taught in a baraita:
A person may not walk to the end of his field
to know what it needs;
phrases.notes: That is, what work to do on it after שבת.

phrases.english: similarly,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוָה שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ לְמָר הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new attack on רבה's idea from Step 25 that silent walking is not preparing.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that making an עירוב by walking, with no words or act, does not count as preparing on יום טוב for שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids walking on שבת when the walk serves a later purpose. This suggests that walking alone can count as forbidden preparation.
